title: The Third Reading

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The third reading is read as the first two were, and the box goes up the road with the difference locked inside. The coat keeps a shape and the seat keeps a hollow; go around the line and leave the crack showing. Nothing under a fold is entered, and the river is not asked.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Vail kiln-house at the going out of Ember

where: Vail kiln-house and Cross, Low Kiln
pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and seven to two hundred and nine days, carried everywhere and told by nobody — six months and twenty-seven days to six months and twenty-nine days, no roof with a word for it. The surgeon's register colours the noticing (a cost asked as a direction answered with the pot and the weather, the carrying arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost, the private file turned out as instruments on a towel, a crowd read as a ninety-second sort with no hand to carry the reading, and an inch of a small hand asked again under a roof the market cannot enter) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line — the old life stays offstage — and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no new hearing, no tenth stopping, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no third telling of the shut counting room, no seventh green, no seventh sighting of the foundling, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read and no ending

scenes.title: The Last Working Week Runs Out
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and the chapter's only drop cap: Day 207, Ember 28, Eighthday, small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof, then before first grey and into the morning. No recap of the one-rhythm inch and no boundary drawn at the turning of the tend. The boy is two hundred and seven days old and six months and twenty-seven days, told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for two hundred and seven days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings, and overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — three counts in three places that do not become one, because agreeing them would want a payer and none stands to any (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that with the sour Ash breath of the unswept corner the house calls the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. One leathery brown-edged crust lies two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool is frozen and unwiped; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting on a warming nobody in this house will perform. In the small hours he lays the file out as instruments on a towel: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth from a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, the told bell beside the heard, the told figure beside the paid, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth, the pale line on a fifth, the held inch on a sixth, and the burned-slate word on its own place beside Jorra's dust and the two shut-room tellings with a hand between them. Sella comes to the fire before the basket and gives the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket, says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar without a touch, feeds him gruel from the house's own dish with the spoon on her sleeve and his mouth unwiped, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed, moves her lips along a two-gapped row without a figure and keeps her finger from beneath the charcoal (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling Tarn keeps six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip, the knife at the edge of its sill and Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to an early and a late thaw while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, and brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, the Seed 16 breath unspent, nine stoppings nine and the loan uncalled (T036/T076). Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground past the bent finger and under the nails, parts dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot You'll do, withholds its full note from a man come up on a wrong wind whose saying stays a saying and costs no pot, and holds his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella's sentence reaches the pot — a remembered repetition, not a change made again (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). The burned-slate word goes around the boards once more and arrives nowhere, no owner, room, hand or reason named, and the boy lays nothing across it (T035/T031). Asked in the morning, the hand goes up an inch toward the note and comes down before the counted breath has finished, filed on its sixth place with no payer named (T061/T082). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no hour since (T058/T079).

scenes.title: The Shape of a Man Who Is Not Named
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 207, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the salt coat and the hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat goes off the high air first and stays longest under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold where one leathery crust keeps its empty place unnamed and no third comes; thread frozen, cold at cheek, temple and wrist, the afterdrop waiting. The household keeps Garl at the very end of the kiln month's last working week in objects and not in a story: the salt-stiff coat holds a broader man's shape with the crease at the left shoulder, the seat keeps its twenty-year leftward lean and hollow, the clean dark line and the new finer grey beside it called the thaw lie unswept, the proverb has gone to the pot, and the debt against a firing of tiles is circled without a name, worse for being uncalled because it can neither be paid nor settled nor stopped (T009/T013/T092). No lesson is made, no collector called, the dead man's name unspoken for two hundred and seven days. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, uncounted and uncopied, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands with the back of the pot counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting required and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079, T100). A neighbour at the door with a cost-question about the firing is sent to the pot and the weather and goes away level, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077). Tarn sweeps the collector's road without once turning along it and no collector comes; nine stoppings stand as nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the seventh nearer its end than ever and not given, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled (T036/T076). Jorra keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, gives the men who went into the back room before first grey no name, and leaves the two shut-room tellings at two with no third while he's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name to the men who burn slates stays ungiven (T035/T031/T065/T095). At the going of the light Sella carries him home at the half-pace, woodsmoke before her in long low bars and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the pan's gone ring, the bare dark trough, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number; the carrying arm is a record in muscle that remembers weight and not cost. Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread frozen (T009/T013/T092/T098). In the small hours the file is laid out and found exact, complete and worth nothing; then the hand goes up an inch toward the river's note and holds for the length of the small intake only, down before the letting go, filed on its sixth place beside the others and never laid across them, not a hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, key, power or rule (T061/T082).

scenes.title: A Second Day of Directions
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 208, Ember 29, Ninthday, small hours under the Vail roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the yard well and the edge of the clay road. The boy is two hundred and eight days old and six months and twenty-eight days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth has had no payer for two hundred and eight days (T088); fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap. The burned-slate word goes around the boards once more, spoken over them and not to the basket: a slate burned in the night in Slate Row, with no owner named, no room, no hand at the flame and no reason, and the voice goes on to the price of barley and the weather. The boy files it again on its own place beside Jorra's dust and the two shut-room tellings with a hand between the three; it is a second telling of a direction and still not a third telling of the shut counting room, not a cause and nothing a clerk could chart (T035/T031/T065/T095, advanced and not paid). Jorra comes through with the day's meal-fine grey dust ground small as meal past the bent finger, goes quieter when the word goes around, speaks to the wheel before anyone (*It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady*), tells a pot You'll do, and knows its full note three turns before it leaves the wheel and withholds it from a man come up on a wrong wind whose saying about a pot singing before its time stays a saying about a pot, with no pot lost and no lesson made (T035/T031, T061/T082). The sweet edge of lead glaze comes up off High Kiln on that wrong wind, touched the fold and went out on the wind that brought it, answered as a direction and entered nowhere; no second edge paid and no cause named in Grathic (T064 held). At the yard well a rack woman with slip dried pale in her wrists asks what the pots will want before the last market and is told to ask the pot and the weather, her question going away level with nothing priced or entered (T077, T058/T079); a man off the clay road keeps his number shut in his fist and pays nothing (T077). Sella's instruction goes to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket; the house, half-pace, jar-glance without a touch, pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed, finger kept from beneath the charcoal, widow's mark untouched (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling Tarn tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to those who want the thaw early and those who want it late, agrees so entirely that no argument can find a foot, and keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went (T036/T076). Asked in the morning, the hand goes up an inch toward the note and comes down at once — the asking is not always answered and there is no failure in the miss — filed on its sixth place with no payer named (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Night Before the Last Market
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 208, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the hearth, the salt coat and the hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending and the heat settles in the low places under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold where one brown-edged crust lies stiff and leathery two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread at his mouth is frozen and unwiped, cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint, and the afterdrop waits on the far side of a warming nobody in this house will perform. Sella moves her lips along a row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, and sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed; the widow's mark is untouched at an afternoon and a dusk, for neither is an opening and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1 (T058/T079, T100). Garl is kept in objects to the last working day: the coat keeps a broader shape, the seat its hollow, the clean dark line and the finer grey their unswept places, the proverb goes to the pot and the debt against the tiles stays neither paid nor settled nor named, with no lesson and no collector (T009/T013/T092). Tarn brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, sweeps past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and over the collector's road without a turn, leaves nine stoppings standing with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled, and no collector comes up or goes down the clay road (T036/T076). Jorra keeps the burned-slate word on its own place beside the dust and the two tellings and makes no cause of it, parts dust from slip, tells a pot You'll do, and when Sella's voice goes low and unfinished at the hearth his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper and holds until the sentence reaches feeding and the end is given to the pot, then moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves the finger standing — a remembered holding and not a change made again, the iron one piece with two bites and no Grathic word for both, joined to no kiln and entered in no slate (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). At the going of the light Sella carries him home around the absences with a wide step and no number and sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, fold right without a look at his face and thread left frozen; the carried fire answers four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for two hundred and eight days, the river keeps its note through the finger's-width door, and the boards keep four nails, four and a knot (T088, T061/T082, T009/T013/T092/T098). In the small hours the file is found exact, complete and worth nothing; then the hand goes up an inch toward the note and stays through the small intake, the hold and the letting go of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch his, and comes down with the breath — the old coordination remembered, not a change made again — filed on its sixth place and laid across nothing (T061/T082).

scenes.title: Four, Four and a Gap Over the Last Market
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 209, Ember 30, Tenthday, the third and last Account-day and the last market of the kiln month. Small hours under the Vail roof, then the morning and the square at the Cross. The boy is two hundred and nine days old and six months and twenty-nine days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth has had no payer for two hundred and nine days (T088); fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). The chapter's one true change is lived and read over the basket: two hundred lean to the reading block under the moot-post while eight pigs go over the wet boards; the bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept beside the told (T078). Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one corner of his mouth, wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure and reads One in twelve, as the notice says low into the top of the crowd — the figure going twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that come late. He says The levy is called. It is not called by me and your house, never I, and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness. The district's arithmetic changes for the third time in the kiln month and cannot be changed back; the printed figure stands unchallenged and a figure read aloud is still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047/T077). Hessa Rale takes the slate up the clay road to Greybank edge-on with the writing turned to her sleeve, her hand arriving at the slate before her eyes arrive at the crowd, a runner and not a reader, answering the question put and not the one behind it; no figure comes off the slate (T080 advanced, not paid). Below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, the market sold over him as water goes over a stone (T090). Sella sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lay and stands half a pace off, giving no instruction and no reason to the basket, and gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket as she carries him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what was read over him (T058/T079). The surgeon's register reads the twice-told figure and the taking of the speaker out of his own sentence as a grammar of charts and signatures; the crowd is sorted in ninety seconds by a man with no hand to carry any of it, and the reading answers nothing for the glaze-room hand carried out on Day 188 — no figure, collector, slate, name, cause or offstage death, and the pale line stays on its own place (T077, T064). The sixth green stays a colour and the foundling a shape; no seventh of either comes at this last market and neither is staged (T050/T051, T033/T034 held). No payer is named and nothing under the fold is entered.

scenes.title: What the Last Day Did Not Enter
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 209, Ember 30, Tenthday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the salt coat and the hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. Ember goes out without a boundary drawn in the narration and neither of the district's two month-names is corrected; the last working week ends and Grain is not named under the roof. The afternoon thins without ending; heat stays longest under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold where one stiff leathery brown-edged crust lies two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped, cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint, the afterdrop waiting. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along a row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, uncounted and uncopied, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079, T100). Garl is kept to the last day without a story: the salt coat on its peg keeps the broader shape and the crease at the left shoulder, the seat keeps its hollow and leftward lean, the clean dark line and the finer grey are gone around with a look and a wide step and not swept, the proverb went to the pot and the debt against the tiles is circled without a name, worse for being uncalled (T009/T013/T092). No lesson made, no collector called, the name unspoken for two hundred and nine days. The widow's mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no shelf, hearth, well, rack, road, basket, yard, market, morning, afternoon or dusk since — no opening in twenty-nine days (T058/T079). Tarn keeps six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, the knife at the very edge of its sill with the unforged collector sentence beside it, told the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, brings the ear-sentence all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, leaves nine stoppings standing with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the seventh nearer its end than ever and still not given, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled, sweeps past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector without once turning along it, and no collector comes; the warm stone lies cold and unreconciled in its unmarked pot in the Debt Loft and the small loft-sill scrape stays on its fourth place (T036/T076, T006). Jorra gives no name to the men who went low into the back room before first grey, comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger and under the nails, parts dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, speaks to the wheel before anyone and tells a pot You'll do, withholds the knowing of its note from a man on a wrong wind whose saying stays a saying and costs no pot, and holds his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella's sentence reaches the pot as a remembered repetition, the iron one piece with two bites joined to no kiln; he's not Vail stays sealed, the promise of the boy's name stays ungiven, the burned-slate word stays a direction arrived nowhere beside the dust and the two tellings with a hand between, and no third telling comes (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). At the going of the light she carries him home around the pan's gone round ring, the bare dark trough, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number, and sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, fold right without a look at his face and thread left frozen (T009/T013/T092/T098). In the small hours he turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds it exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid, nine stoppings with no tenth, three held changes on three places with the loft scrape on a fourth, the pale line on a fifth and the held inch on a sixth with all its answers, the burned-slate word on its own place, and the crust's gap, the shelf's two gaps, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch — no third gap, no fourth likeness, no finger of his drawn across them (T061/T082, T100, T060/T086/T097). Then he puts the question to his hand. Sella has gone to her own bed and left the coals to keep themselves and there is no breathing number anywhere in the house, only the rhythm through the door. The hand goes up an inch toward the note of water over water and comes down at once against the fold: under the very conditions that gave the one-rhythm holding on Day 206 the body answers with a miss this time, and the asking is not always answered and there is no failure in the miss. He files it on the sixth place beside the others, not a longer reach, stronger hand, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, one of the three held changes, key, power or rule, no payer named to it and nothing standing up out of it to call itself a sign (T061/T082 advanced and not paid). He still cannot close the two inches to the pot handle, lift his chin the two inches to the crust or speak a number that anybody under any roof has been asked to believe. The hand stays down against the fold; two hundred and nine stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody under any roof; the carried fire's fifth has had no payer for two hundred and nine days; the stone lies cold in its loft pot, the charcoal unread, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan that can hear uncalled; the seventh year stands nearer its end than it has ever stood and has not given. Nothing has been joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, and Ember goes out without a boundary drawn while the count goes forward into Day 210, Grain 1, Firstday.
